\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ثريا} (thurayyā)}{ثريا (thurayyā)}]{\ar{ثريا} (thurayyā) — a chandelier}

\label{lesson:AR-C550-thurayya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bolt, then the Arabic for a drain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ثريا}}
\textbf{\ar{ثريا}} — \emph{thurayyā} — \textquotedblleft{}a chandelier\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{غرفة} \ar{الجلوس} \ar{ثريا} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī ghurfat al-julūs thurayyā kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a big chandelier in the sitting room.
\end{quote}

\ar{الثريا} is also the Pleiades, a cluster of stars.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ثريا}} (\emph{thurayyā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-r-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be many, to abound\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives al-thurayyā as the Pleiades, a cluster of many stars, and a cluster of lamps.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thurayyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thurayyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī ghurfat al-julūs thurayyā kabīra.} — There is a big chandelier in the sitting room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a bolt, then the Arabic for a drain, then say \emph{thurayyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ثريا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A chandelier\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مزهرية} (mazhariyya)}{مزهرية (mazhariyya)}]{\ar{مزهرية} (mazhariyya) — a vase}

\label{lesson:AR-C550-mazhariyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a drain, then the Arabic for a chandelier.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مزهرية}}
\textbf{\ar{مزهرية}} — \emph{mazhariyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a vase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وضعت} \ar{أمي} \ar{الورد} \ar{في} \ar{المزهرية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waḍaʿat ummī al-ward fī al-mazhariyya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother put the roses in the vase.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مزهرية}} (\emph{mazhariyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{z-h-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to shine; a flower\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Zahra, a flower, which you know, is from the same root: a mazhariyya is a thing for flowers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a drain, then the Arabic for a chandelier, then say \emph{mazhariyya} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نفض} (nafaḍa)}{نفض (nafaḍa)}]{\ar{نفض} (nafaḍa) — to shake out (dust)}

\label{lesson:AR-C550-nafada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a chandelier, then the Arabic for a vase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نفض}}
\textbf{\ar{نفض}} — \emph{nafaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to shake out (dust)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نفضت} \ar{أمي} \ar{السجادة} \ar{في} \ar{الشرفة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nafaḍat ummī as-sajjāda fī ash-shurfa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother shook out the carpet on the balcony.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينفض}, \emph{yanfuḍ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نفض}} (\emph{nafaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-f-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to shake a thing to clear it\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives nafaḍa, aor. yanfuḍu, as to shake a cloth so that what is on it falls off.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لمع} (lammaʿa)}{لمع (lammaʿa)}]{\ar{لمع} (lammaʿa) — to polish}

\label{lesson:AR-C550-lammaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a vase, then the Arabic for to shake out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لمع}}
\textbf{\ar{لمع}} — \emph{lammaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to polish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لمع} \ar{أبي} \ar{حذاءه} \ar{قبل} \ar{الحفلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lammaʿa abī ḥidhāʾahu qabla al-ḥafla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father polished his shoes before the party.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يلمع}, \emph{yulammiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لمع}} (\emph{lammaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-m-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to shine, to gleam\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lāmiʿ, shiny, which you know, is from the same root; Form II is to make a thing shine.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صان} (ṣāna)}{صان (ṣāna)}]{\ar{صان} (ṣāna) — to maintain, to look after (a thing)}

\label{lesson:AR-C550-sana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to shake out, then the Arabic for to polish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صان}}
\textbf{\ar{صان}} — \emph{ṣāna} — \textquotedblleft{}to maintain, to look after (a thing)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يصون} \ar{جدي} \ar{ساعته} \ar{القديمة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaṣūnu jaddī sāʿatahu al-qadīma.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather takes care of his old watch.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصون}, \emph{yaṣūn}.

The noun \ar{صيانة} is maintenance.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صان}} (\emph{ṣāna}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-w-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to preserve, to guard\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives ṣāna, aor. yaṣūnu, as to keep a thing safe.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
